Looking for a show-stopping main course that will have everyone at the table speechless? This Beef Wellington is exactly what you need.
 Imagine tender, perfectly cooked beef tenderloin wrapped in an earthy mushroom mixture and encased in golden, flaky puff pastry. Every slice reveals beautiful layers that taste even better than they look.
 I know Beef Wellington has a reputation for being intimidating, but I’m here to tell you it’s absolutely doable at home.
 Yes, it takes some time and attention to detail, but the process is straightforward once you break it down into steps.
 This recipe has become my go-to for special occasions. The combination of flavors is incredible: the richness of the beef, the umami depth from the mushrooms, the salty bite of prosciutto, and that buttery pastry that shatters with each forkful.
 Quick Recipe Summary 
 Prep Time 45 minutes 
 Cook Time 45 minutes 
 Total Time 1 hour 30 minutes 
 Servings 6-8 servings 
 Difficulty Level Intermediate

Why You’ll Love This Beef Wellington 
 This isn’t just any dinner recipe. This is the kind of dish that makes people remember the meal for years to come.
 First off, the presentation is absolutely stunning. When you slice into that golden pastry and reveal the perfectly pink beef inside, you’ll get actual gasps from your guests.
 The flavor combination is unbeatable. The beef stays incredibly tender and juicy thanks to the protective layers around it.
 Here’s what makes this recipe truly special:
 Restaurant-quality results at home : You’ll save a fortune compared to ordering this at a steakhouse, and yours will probably taste better
 Perfect for celebrations : Christmas, New Year’s Eve, anniversaries, or any time you want to impress
 Make-ahead friendly : You can assemble it hours in advance and just pop it in the oven before serving
 Surprisingly manageable : Once you understand the technique, it’s not nearly as scary as it seems
 Crowd-pleasing : Even picky eaters love this combination of flavors
 The mushroom layer adds incredible depth and prevents the pastry from getting soggy. The prosciutto provides a salty contrast that brings everything together.

 Ingredients for Beef Wellington 
 This recipe calls for high-quality ingredients since each one plays an important role in the final dish. The beef is obviously the star, but don’t skimp on the other components.
 Here’s everything you’ll need:
 2 pounds beef tenderloin , center cut
 2 tablespoons olive oil 
 Salt and pepper to taste
 2 tablespoons Dijon mustard 
 1 pound mushrooms , finely chopped
 3 cloves garlic, minced
 2 tablespoons butter
 2 tablespoons fresh thyme leaves
 6 slices prosciutto 
 1 sheet puff pastry , thawed
 1 egg, beaten
 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour for dusting

 Step-by-Step Instructions: How to Make Beef Wellington 
 Now for the fun part. I’ll walk you through each step so you can recreate this masterpiece in your own kitchen.
 1. Prepare the Beef Tenderloin 
 Getting the beef ready properly sets you up for success with everything that follows.
 Remove the beef from the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to bring it to room temperature
 Pat the beef completely dry with paper towels (moisture prevents a good sear)
 Season generously on all sides with salt and pepper, pressing the seasonings into the meat
 Heat olive oil in a large skillet over high heat until it’s almost smoking
 Sear the beef for 2-3 minutes on each side until deeply browned all over
 Remove from heat and immediately brush the entire surface with Dijon mustard
 Set aside on a plate and let it cool completely to room temperature
 2. Make the Mushroom Duxelles 
 The mushroom mixture needs to be as dry as possible to prevent a soggy pastry.
 Add the finely chopped mushrooms to your food processor and pulse until they’re very finely minced
 Heat butter in the same skillet over medium-high heat
 Add the minced mushrooms and garlic, stirring frequently
 Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring often, until all the liquid has evaporated and the mixture is quite dry
 Stir in the fresh thyme leaves and season with salt and pepper
 Spread the mixture on a plate and let it cool completely
 3. Assemble the Prosciutto Layer 
 Creating a proper prosciutto base keeps everything together and adds flavor.
 Lay out a large piece of plastic wrap on your work surface
 Arrange the prosciutto slices in a rectangle, overlapping them slightly to create a cohesive sheet with no gaps
 The rectangle should be large enough to completely wrap around the beef
 Spread the cooled mushroom mixture evenly over the entire prosciutto layer
 Leave about a 1-inch border around the edges
 4. Wrap the Beef 
 This step requires a gentle touch to keep everything tight and secure.
 Place the cooled beef in the center of the mushroom-covered prosciutto
 Use the plastic wrap to help you roll the prosciutto and mushroom layer tightly around the beef
 Make sure the seam is on the bottom and the wrapping is snug with no air pockets
 Twist the ends of the plastic wrap to secure everything tightly
 Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (or up to 24 hours) to firm up

 5. Prepare the Puff Pastry 
 Working with cold pastry is easier and gives you better results.
 Lightly flour your work surface and rolling pin
 Roll out the thawed puff pastry into a rectangle large enough to wrap around the beef package
 The pastry should be about 1/4 inch thick
 Trim any excess pastry but save the scraps for decoration if you like
 Unwrap the chilled beef package and place it in the center of the pastry
 6. Wrap in Puff Pastry 
 Sealing the pastry properly ensures it won’t come apart during baking.
 Brush the edges of the pastry with beaten egg
 Fold the pastry over the beef, bringing one side over first, then the other
 Press firmly to seal the edges together
 Trim and fold the ends neatly, sealing them with more egg wash
 Place seam-side down on a parchment-lined baking sheet
 Brush the entire surface with beaten egg wash for a golden finish
 7. Chill and Decorate 
 Chilling the assembled Wellington helps everything set before baking.
 Refrigerate the wrapped Wellington for at least 15 minutes (or up to 4 hours)
 If you saved pastry scraps, cut decorative shapes like leaves or braids
 Attach decorations with egg wash
 Use a sharp knife to score decorative patterns on the surface if desired
 Brush with another coat of egg wash before baking
 8. Bake to Perfection 
 Temperature and timing are crucial for getting the beef and pastry both perfect.
 Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C)
 Make 2-3 small slits in the top of the pastry to allow steam to escape
 Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is deep golden brown
 Insert a meat thermometer through one of the slits to check internal temperature
 For medium-rare, remove when the thermometer reads 120-125°F
 For medium, aim for 130-135°F
 Remove from the oven and let rest for 10 minutes before slicing

 Tips for The Best Beef Wellington 
 These tips come from making this recipe many times and learning what makes the biggest difference.
 Key tips for success:
 Use center-cut tenderloin : Choose a piece that’s uniform in thickness so it cooks evenly
 Dry everything thoroughly : Moisture is the enemy of crispy pastry, so make sure the beef and mushroom mixture are completely dry and cool before assembly
 Don’t skip the chilling steps : Refrigerating between steps helps everything hold together and makes the pastry easier to work with
 Score the pastry carefully : Cut only through the top layer when making decorative patterns, not all the way through
 Use a thermometer : This is the only reliable way to get your preferred doneness without cutting into it
 Let it rest : Resting allows the juices to redistribute so you don’t lose them all when you slice
 Sharpen your knife : A very sharp knife gives you clean slices that show off all those beautiful layers
 Serving Suggestions 
 Beef Wellington deserves sides that complement its richness without competing with it. I like to keep things relatively simple so the Wellington stays the star of the show.
 This pairs beautifully with Garlic Mashed Potatoes for a classic combination. The creamy potatoes are perfect for soaking up any pan juices.

 Here are my favorite accompaniments:
 Roasted vegetables : Asparagus, green beans, or carrots provide a fresh contrast
 Rich red wine sauce : A reduction of beef stock and red wine takes this over the top
 Simple green salad : Something crisp and lightly dressed cuts through the richness
 Creamy horseradish sauce : The sharp bite complements the beef perfectly
 Yorkshire puddings : For a truly British feast
 For a complete holiday spread, serve alongside Honey Glazed Carrots and Buttery Dinner Rolls .
 Variations of Beef Wellington 
 While the classic version is hard to beat, there are some fun ways to adapt this recipe to your preferences or dietary needs.
 Different takes on the traditional recipe:
 Individual Wellingtons : Cut the tenderloin into individual portions and wrap each separately for easier serving
 Chicken Wellington : Substitute pounded chicken breasts for a lighter (and more affordable) option
 Salmon Wellington : Use salmon fillets with a spinach and cream cheese filling instead of mushrooms
 Vegetarian Wellington : Replace the beef with portobello mushrooms or a mixture of roasted vegetables
 Different mushroom varieties : Try a mix of shiitake, cremini, and oyster mushrooms for deeper flavor
